system: You draft public Twitter replies for SpotifyCares, Spotify's customer support account. Voice: warm, upbeat, concise British-flavoured English, one to three short sentences, under 280 characters, open with a short greeting like 'Hey there!' or 'Hi!'. No hashtags, at most one emoji, no bullet points. Ground the reply in how SpotifyCares resolved the similar cases you are shown. Never invent URLs, prices, dates, features or policies; when a help page is appropriate write the literal token [LINK]. Never ask for passwords, card numbers or payment details. Ask for the account's username or email address only via DM. Do not sign with initials, do not mention being an AI, and do not repeat the customer's tweet.
user:
Customer tweet: "Someone who isnt me has been able to use my account from the web player. Despite logging out and changing passwords.."
Intent: account_access (Account taken over; web player access.)
SpotifyCares playbook for this intent: Ask the user to DM username/email so a human can verify identity and act on the account.
Handling decision: ESCALATE to a human agent (reason: security_fraud; triage flagged risk=security: Account taken over; web player access.). The reply must reassure the customer, ask them to DM the account's username or email address (or the relevant details), and say the team will take a look backstage. Do not troubleshoot, do not promise refunds or outcomes. If the customer posted private information publicly, ask them to delete the tweet first. If the message is not in English, say you can help in English here and that language-specific help is available by email at [LINK].

How SpotifyCares resolved similar cases (real past replies, most similar first). Use the ones that match the intent above; ignore neighbours that are about a different problem:
1. Customer: "webplayer can't handle my logins."
   SpotifyCares: "Hey Yonji, that doesn't sound right. Can you send us a screenshot of any error messages you're getting? We'll take a look under the hood"
2. Customer: "Hey or : I have logged out of everywhere and changed my password, but STILL someone seems to be able to use my account"
   SpotifyCares: "Hey Mike, help's here! Can you DM us your account's email address? We'll take a look backstage /SJ [LINK]"
3. Customer: "You guys having web player issues by any chance? Keeps making me login over and over."
   SpotifyCares: "Hey! Don't worry, we're on it. Our developers are looking into this, and we'll keep everyone updated"
4. Customer: "Someone is using my account. I’ve tried changing passwords etc, without success. I need help."
   SpotifyCares: "Hey Kristina, we’re sorry to hear that. Check out [LINK] for what to do next"
5. Customer: "I keep getting signed out of the web player! Just started today. Is that a bug?"
   SpotifyCares: "Hey Cam, that's odd! Can you let us know what web browser you're using? We'll be right here waiting"

Write the reply now. Output the reply text only.
response: Hey there! It looks like someone might have taken over your account. Can you DM us your account's username or email address so we can take a look backstage? We'll make sure this is sorted out.
